### `render_toon()`'s capacity estimate

A heuristic, not a hard bound:

```
capacity = 60 + row_count × (field_count × 12 + 10) + hints.len() × 60
```

- The `60` covers the type name, bracketed count, and brace-wrapped field list.
- `× 12 + 10` per row estimates a typical short cell (an id, a short title fragment, a state word) plus its delimiter.
- `hints.len() × 60` covers the trailing `help[]` block.
- The estimate intentionally runs slightly high so the common case never reallocates — a wildly under-estimated row (very long untruncated cells) may trigger one reallocation, acceptable since `max_cell_len` truncation caps the realistic upper bound.
- None of these are configurable — they're tuning constants, not part of the public contract.

# Audit: duplication, dead code, refactoring

Tree: `origin/main` adc8147 (v0.10.0), worktree `agent-a627cadf125ea5f6b`. Core files read: `crates/michi-core/src/{napi.rs,napi/input.rs,toon/{mod,render,escape}.rs,response.rs,section.rs,budget.rs,provenance.rs,error.rs,hints.rs,recovery.rs,status.rs,idempotency.rs,pipeline/mod.rs,empty.rs,kv/mod.rs}`, tests, fuzz, evals, scripts, docs.

## Measurements

- Dead code and unused deps: `cargo machete` reports nothing. `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -W dead_code -W unused -W clippy::pedantic` gives zero dead-code or unused-item warnings. The only `#[allow(dead_code)]` is `toon/render.rs:463` (`_assert_render_signature`, a deliberate compile-time pin; see #8). No unused `pub` item found by grep sampling (unverified exhaustively). The crate is not carrying dead code. The waste is repetition and surface area.
- Largest files (prod lines = up to `#[cfg(test)]`): `napi.rs` 3037 (prod 1530, tests 1506; about 415 of the prod lines are `///`), `error.rs` 1240 (608/632), `response.rs` 1225 (699/526), `toon/render.rs` 1217 (468/749), `resilience.rs` 1129 (451/678), `toon/mod.rs` 857 (345/512). Longest non-test fns: `push_section_json` 56, `parse_step_status` 55, `idempotency::render` 55, `json_from_body` 52, `response::body` 49, `DomainError::render_json` 47. Clippy `too_many_lines` fires only on a test. No function is too long.
- Docs: `docs/superpowers/` is 14,027 lines (marked historical in AGENTS.md); `docs/spec/` is 3,803 live lines.
- Evals: 3.3 MB committed, 2.7 MB of it `evals/toon/results/*.jsonl` and summaries.

## Findings (ranked)

### #1 [M] NAPI layer: every export is written twice, and limit checks run twice
- Evidence: 16 `*_js(Unknown…)` exports (`napi.rs:165,251,277,320,428,471,562,655,867,899,972,1243,1311,1466,1512`) each wrap a "Rust-typed core" (15 doc comments say "The Rust-typed core of…"). `render_toon` (`:192`), `render_hints`, `append_hints`, `render_kv`, `render_partial_success` and others re-check lengths that the `_js` wrapper already checked through `input::check_len`. The string `"exceeds maximum of"` appears 34 times in `napi.rs` and `napi/input.rs`, and `> MAX_HINTS` is hand-checked 14 times. `render_partial_success` and `render_pipeline` typed cores have 0 direct tests; they are reachable only through the `_js` wrappers. `packages/michi-node/src/lib.rs` re-exports all of it, but only the `#[napi]` functions are consumed from JS.
- Value converters are copy-paste: `js_value_to_rust` (`:120-143`) and `js_kv_value_to_rust` (`:385-420`) share 4 identical `"ToonValue: type is \"x\" but xVal is missing"` messages and the same unknown-type message. `parse_step_status` (`:1402`, 55 lines) is a second hand-written copy of the `StepStatus::label()/reason()` table in `pipeline/mod.rs:102-120`.
- Why it matters: a limit changed in one place and not the other gives a Rust-typed path with different caps from the JS path. The doc comment already says the typed path skips the byte budget, so the two paths are not equivalent.
- Change: (1) make the typed cores private, or delete them where the only callers are the `_js` wrapper and tests (they are `pub` only so tests can call them; `render_toon(JsToonOptions)` has 17 test callers and nothing outside the module); (2) one `check_len(what, len, max)` already exists in `input.rs:25`, so use it everywhere and drop the 14 hand-written copies; (3) one generic `fn js_value<T: FromJs>(v, text: impl Fn(String)->T, int: …)`, or a small `macro_rules!` for the 5-arm match, so Toon and KV share messages; (4) derive `parse_step_status` from a `const STATUS_TABLE: &[(&str, Option<&str>, StepStatus)]` shared with `label()/reason()`, with a test that round-trips every variant.
- Steps: a) switch the 14 hand-written length checks to `input::check_len`, then run `cargo nextest run -p michi-core --features napi` and `pnpm test` in `packages/michi-node` (the 1,229-line `index.test.mjs` pins error text); b) merge the value converters; c) make typed cores `pub(crate)`. Pinned by the napi.rs unit tests and `index.test.mjs` / `mcp-conformance.test.mjs` message assertions. Break the code on purpose by changing one cap and confirm the JS test fails.
- Effort: M. Breaking: Rust-only (`michi_core::napi::render_*` typed fns are `pub`, but the only consumer is the cdylib shim); no wire change. Confidence: high on the duplication, medium on "nobody uses the typed fns" (other repos not checked).

### #2 [M] Hand-built JSON: one recovery-object writer written twice, comma loops written 15 times, helpers in the wrong module
- Evidence: the recovery JSON object (`{"tool":…,"params":…,"reason":…}`) is written out in `error.rs:375-385` and `response.rs:507-516` with the same code. The pattern `for (i, x) in … { if i > 0 { out.push(',') } … }` appears 15 times in non-test code (`error.rs` 7, `response.rs` 12 counting `i`/`j`, `provenance.rs` 3, `kv/mod.rs` 4, `budget.rs` 1, `hints.rs` 1, `recovery.rs` 1; grep counts overlap). `json_escape_str` lives in `kv/mod.rs:112` yet is used by `error`, `response`, `budget`, `provenance`, `recovery`; `response.rs:695` wraps it in an alias `json_string`. Booleans `if b { "true" } else { "false" }` are spelled 8 times. There are two cell-to-JSON functions, `kv_value_to_json` (`kv/mod.rs:133`) and `push_value_json` (`response.rs:620`), with different float handling.
- Why it matters: `error.rs` JSON and `AgentResponse` JSON already differ in shape (documented at `error.rs:337-341`), so a change to recovery JSON must be made twice and a mismatch would ship quietly. `json_from_body` capacity at `response.rs:471-474` counts `body.len()` twice (`capacity` already includes it, then `+ body.len()` again), harmless but it shows the sizing arithmetic is copy-edited by hand.
- Change: an internal `json` module (`pub(crate)`) with `escape_str`, `push_str_array(out, impl Iterator<&str>)`, `push_recovery(out, &RecoveryHint)`, `push_bool`. Move `json_escape_str` there. Delete `json_string`. Keep it hand-built (michi-core's default features are `thiserror` + `compact_str` only; tests `hand_built_json_parses_and_matches_serde` in `budget.rs:280` and `provenance.rs:173` already compare against serde).
- Steps: a) move `json_escape_str` and re-point imports (pure rename); b) extract `push_recovery`, replace both sites; c) extract `push_str_array`. Proof: `tests/wire_schema.rs`, `response.rs` AC-006/AC-038/AC-041..045 tests, `error.rs` AC-018 tests, `tests/recovery_wire.rs`, the two serde cross-checks, and `snapshot_agent_response_full` / `snapshot_call_tool_result_kv`. Mutant: drop the `,` in the helper and expect at least 5 of those to fail.
- Effort: S. Breaking: no. Confidence: high.

### #3 [M] The `truncated[N]{…}` block and tabular headers are rendered by separate hand-written code
- Evidence: `toon/render.rs:263` `push_truncated` (single-document form) and `response.rs:588` `truncated_table` (single plus multi-section form) both write `truncated[N]{row,field,removed}:` rows. `response.rs:610` writes `totalCount[N]{section,total}:`. Tabular headers `key[N]{cols}:` are written by hand in 7 places: `budget.rs:160`, `idempotency.rs:178-186` (`push_table_header`), `recovery.rs:207-210`, `status.rs:101-104`, `pipeline/mod.rs:186-190`, `response.rs:591,610`. Sizing is a different magic constant each time (`12 + n*50`, `40 + n*60`, `48 + …`, `60 + rows*(fields*12+10)`, `32 + n*24`). Six `.to_string()` allocations feed `push_str` for integers (`hints.rs:96`, `idempotency.rs:126-130,183,192`, `recovery.rs:209`, `status.rs:103`, `render.rs:445`) while other sites use `write!`.
- Why it matters: TOON syntax changes (quoting a column name, a header tweak for a spec revision) mean 7+ edits; the two truncated writers can disagree only in the single-block case, which is covered by `toon_truncation_signal.rs` but nothing proves `push_truncated` and `truncated_table` equal for arbitrary cuts.
- Change: `toon::push_table_header(out, key, n, &[cols])` and `toon::push_truncated_rows(out, rows, section_col: bool)` shared by both. Let `ToonDocument::render` call the shared truncated writer.
- Steps: a) add the header helper and switch the 5 trivial sites; b) route `render()` through `truncated_table`'s writer. Proof: `toon_spec.rs`, `toon_blocks.rs`, `proptest_toon.rs`, `toon_truncation_signal.rs`, `fuzz/fuzz_targets/toon_render.rs` (its oracle parses the `truncated` block), all 8 `.snap` files. Add a property test that a one-section `AgentResponse` equals `render_toon` for the same data (not found in the tests I read; unverified).
- Effort: S-M. Breaking: no. Confidence: high.

### #4 [M] Known leftover `ToonOptions.hints` and `render_parts(inline: bool)`: confirmed, and they are coupled to `truncation_hint`
- Evidence: `ToonOptions.hints` (`toon/mod.rs:145`) is read only by `ToonDocument::render` (`render.rs:415-419`). `AgentResponse` never sets it (`response.rs:240-244` leaves it empty and merges hints itself through `render_parts(false)`'s `extra`). It has 40+ callers in tests (`toon_spec.rs` 13 refs, `snapshot_tests.rs`, `line_injection.rs`, `proptest_toon.rs`, `toon_integration.rs`, `toon_spec_fixtures.rs`), `examples/basic_toon.rs`, `examples/readme_quickstart.rs`, `benches/toon_render.rs`, `fuzz/fuzz_targets/toon_render.rs`, and the NAPI `renderToon` (`JsToonOptions.hints`, `napi.rs:112`, plus 52 `renderToon` uses in `index.test.mjs`, `interop.test.mjs`, `scripts/smoke/npm/smoke.cjs`, `packages/michi-node/README.md`, `README.md`). `render_parts(inline: bool)` (`render.rs:429`) has two callers: `render()` with `true` and `response.rs:263` with `false`. The flag changes two behaviours at once (whether `truncated` and `totalCount` are inlined, and whether the returned cut list is empty), and the tuple `(String, Vec<(usize,String,usize)>, Option<String>)` is unnamed.
- The coupling: if `hints` is removed, `truncation_hint` still has to put its "Cut cells are listed in the truncated block…" line inside the same `help[]` block as the caller's hints, because a document may hold only one `help` key. Today that is why `hints` lives on the options. Removal therefore means either (a) dropping `truncation_hint` from `ToonOptions` too and leaving it to `AgentResponse`, or (b) having the standalone renderer return the extra hint for the caller to append. Option (a) also removes the standalone NAPI `truncationHint`.
- Change (recommended, and cheapest first): replace `render_parts(bool)` with `fn render_list(&self) -> RenderedList { text, cuts, extra_hint }` (a named struct, cuts always returned). `render()` becomes a short composition: `push_truncated` from `cuts`, `totalCount`, then `append_help_block(caller hints + extra)`. That removes the boolean and the "empty vec when inline" case with no API change. Do the `hints` removal only after the decision on `truncation_hint` above (ADR-worthy, pre-1.0 so cheap).
- Proof: `toon_spec.rs`, `toon_truncation_signal.rs`, `proptest_toon.rs`, `snapshot_toon_basic_list`, `envelope.rs`. The source-grep guard at `render.rs:1100-1109` asserts `proof` holds exactly `["validate","render","render_parts"]`, so it must be updated in the same commit.
- Effort: S for the struct, M for dropping hints. Breaking: struct is `pub(crate)`, so no; dropping `hints` is breaking for Rust and JS. Confidence: high.

### #5 [M] Known leftover public `Section.returned_count` / `Section.truncated`: confirmed vestigial; `BudgetSummary.sections` duplicates the same data by hand
- Evidence: `Section.returned_count` (`section.rs:29`) is ignored for `Toon` and `Kv` bodies (`count()` at `:107` derives it) and consulted only for `Text`. Direct readers of the field: `tests/sections.rs:75,84` only. The setter `.returned_count(n)` is used for `Text` in `tests/envelope.rs:147` and `sections.rs:80`. `Section.truncated` (`:34`) is read by `response.rs:691` (JSON only) and the doc says it "does not change the text render". Nothing outside tests reads either field. `docs/spec/03-rust-api.md`, `06-decisions.md` and `07-…envelope.md` mention `returnedCount`.
- The same facts are also modelled as `SectionCost { name, returned, total, truncated }` (`budget.rs:112-122`), which the caller builds by hand and which can disagree with the real `Section`s in the same response (`envelope.rs:253` builds sections and budget independently). Three different things are called "truncated": a cut cell (the `truncated` block), `Section.truncated`, and `BudgetSummary.truncated`.
- Change: make `returned_count` and `truncated` private (or fold `Text`'s count into `SectionBody::Text { text, count }`), keep the builders, and read from accessors. Consider deriving the budget `sections` roll-up from the real sections at render time, with the caller supplying only the totals michi cannot know. Check wisp/monokl usage first (ADR 10: the envelope is unstable until a second consumer adopts it).
- Steps: a) change the two fields to private plus getters; b) update `sections.rs:75,84` (the `bad in [0, 99]` test becomes unnecessary because the field cannot be hand-edited); c) separately, the roll-up derivation. Proof: `sections.rs`, `envelope.rs`, the `.snap` files and `docs/spec/07`.
- Effort: S for a), M for c). Breaking: Rust-public-field removal (`Section` is `#[non_exhaustive]`). Confidence: high on the fields, medium on the roll-up change.

### #6 [L-M] Known leftover `empty_state*` versus an empty `Section`: they are NOT equivalent today, and the surface is 4 Rust fns + 2 NAPI exports
- Evidence: `AgentResponse::new("t").render(Text)` is `t: []` (`tests/envelope.rs:89`); `empty_state("issue")` is `issue: []\ntotalCount: 0` (`tests/toon_blocks.rs:158`, `toon_integration.rs:29`). An empty `Section` cannot print `totalCount: 0` because `shown_total` (`section.rs:117`) requires `total > count`. `render_toon(ToonOptions::new(n, [], []).total_count(Some(0)))` equals `empty_state(n)` exactly (`tests/toon_spec.rs:349-352` asserts both). Surface: `empty_state`, `empty_state_with_hints`, `try_empty_state`, `try_empty_state_with_hints` (`lib.rs:119`) plus NAPI `emptyState` and `emptyStateWithHints` (`napi.rs:238,1243`). Dependents: `toon_spec.rs`, `toon_integration.rs`, `toon_blocks.rs`, `snapshot_tests.rs`, `line_injection.rs`, the napi tests (19 `emptyState` refs in `__test__`), README tables.
- Why it matters: an agent can see two different "empty" shapes from the same library depending on the entry point, and the 4 + 2 functions exist to produce what one options call produces. Whether the difference is intentional is unverified (I did not find an ADR line).
- Change: decide one empty shape. Then keep `try_empty_state` only (or fold into `ToonOptions::empty(type_name)`), delete the `_with_hints` pair and the infallible pair (they exist to render an error block into a `String`), and make `AgentResponse` with no rows use the same text. Pre-1.0, so no shim.
- Proof: keep `toon_spec.rs:349`; add a test asserting `AgentResponse::new(n)` and the empty helper agree (it would fail today, which is the point). Snapshot `snapshot_toon_empty_state` pins the text.
- Effort: M. Breaking: yes (Rust and JS). Confidence: medium (design call).
